stages.title: Identify canonical works for this topic before broad recall
instructions: Before any broad literature search runs, name the specific canonical or landmark works a domain expert would expect this exact paper to engage with: foundational terminology sources, seminal papers, the most important recent high-impact systems, key surveys, and known counterexamples. Generate these dynamically from the topic and brief — never reuse a fixed list carried over from a different paper's topic.

Write ONLY research/landmark-candidates.json: {version:1,candidates:[{name,why_canonical,expected_identifiers?:{arxiv_id?,doi?},confidence:high|medium|low}]}. Name real, verifiable works only; omit expected_identifiers rather than inventing one when uncertain of the exact id. List 5 to 30 candidates ordered by confidence.

The release-gated canonical set is paper-scale: output at most 20 candidates, ordered by genuine canonical importance. Reserve high confidence for works that this exact paper would be academically deficient not to discuss; adjacent examples and general benchmarks are medium or low rather than automatically high.

stages.title: Search planning
instructions: Write strict JSON matching {"version":1,"topic":"...","query_variants":[...],"taxonomy_cells":[{"cell":"...","query_variants":["...","...","..."]}],"exclusion_terms":[],"venue_priorities":[],"source_types":[...]}. Preserve every project taxonomy coverage cell verbatim as a taxonomy_cells[].cell; each cell must have at least 3 distinct query variants.
Cover method families, evaluation/benchmark terms, prior surveys, and application variants. Prefer queries that can retrieve both recent and foundational work.

research/landmark-candidates.json names the specific canonical/landmark works this survey is expected to engage with. Add at least one query_variant per higher-confidence candidate that targets it by name, author, or distinctive terminology rather than only the general topic, so broad recall is likely to actually surface each named landmark.

stages.title: Analyze the pinned repository architecture
instructions: Read the pinned repository context as software evidence and write ONLY evidence/codebase-analysis.raw.json. Cover every codebase in codebases/manifest.json; do not execute code, infer benchmark results, or treat repository claims as independently validated scientific evidence.

Schema: {version:1,codebases:[{codebase_id,summary,summary_locators,components:[{id,name,summary,locators}],entrypoints:[{id,name,summary,locators}],interfaces:[{from,to,relationship,summary,locators}],data_control_flows:[{summary,locators}],configuration_extension_points:[{id,name,summary,locators}],trust_boundaries:[{summary,locators}],operational_limitations:[{summary,locators}]}]}. All arrays are required; use [] when the bounded snapshot does not support that category. Include at least one component per codebase.

Every summary, component, entrypoint, interface, flow, extension point, trust boundary, and limitation must cite one or more exact markers copied verbatim from evidence/codebase-context.md, for example `[codebase:repo:path/file.ts#L1-L40]`. A limitation must be an observed constraint in the supplied code/config/docs, not an argument from missing evidence. Preserve uncertainty and do not invent files, line ranges, components, relationships, or behavior.

stages.title: Compare pinned repositories as software evidence
instructions: Write ONLY evidence/codebase-comparison.raw.json as {version:1,codebases:[{codebase_id,purpose,architecture_summary,license,extension_points,limitations,locators}],comparisons:[{dimension,codebase_ids,synthesis,locators}]}. Cover every pinned codebase exactly once. Use license:null when the pinned evidence does not establish a license.

Every row must use exact locators copied from the validated architecture dossier/context. When two or more codebases are pinned, add at least one comparison that names all compared IDs and includes at least one exact locator from each. Compare purpose, component boundaries, interfaces, extension model, trust boundaries, or documented operational limitations—not stars, popularity, or inferred benchmark quality.
codebases/mentioned-repositories.json is a bounded operator candidate list only. Do not treat an unpinned mentioned repository as evidence, add it to the comparison, recursively fetch it, or cite it.

stages.title: Reserve landmark targets and publish what is still unretrieved
Outline
instructions: When feedback/outline-revision.md is present, treat it as the human's requested changes for this outline revision. Implement it while preserving the evidence-first scope and emit matching outline.md and outline.json.

Every outline.json section MUST include: id, title, role, target_words, purpose, keywords (at least two strings), and source_ids. keywords are the retrieval terms used for its section evidence packet.

For a survey contract, assign exactly these role values where applicable: introduction_gap_contributions, multi_axis_taxonomy, method_family (at least two sections), related_work_differentiation, limitations_future_work, or body. Include each required role at least once, and use body only for remaining sections.

Configured repositories are pinned codebase evidence, not scholarly literature. Use evidence/codebase-analysis.json as the validated architecture dossier and inspect its exact file/line locators before making a repository claim. Cite `[codebase:<id>]` or `[codebase:<id>:path#Lx-Ly]`; never claim execution results unless a verified empirical result artifact is supplied.

This is a repository-study paper: organize the argument around the pinned system's problem framing, architecture, component responsibilities, interfaces/workflows, design trade-offs, operational boundaries, and limitations. Explain the solution; do not turn the paper into a file-by-file inventory or infer behavior that the pinned evidence does not show.

stages.title: Plan placed figures and tables
instructions: Write strict JSON with version:1 and placements:[{id,placement:{section_id,discussion}}]. Select no artifact unless it makes a specific argument easier to understand. You—not a preset menu—choose the reader question, visual form, placement, and supporting sources. A legacy concept_map remains supported, but prefer diagrams:[{id,title,caption,insight,placement:{section_id,discussion},source_ids:[existing classified source ids],layout?:{kind:grid,columns:1|2|3}|{kind:flow,direction:left_to_right|top_to_bottom},nodes:[{id,label}],edges:[{from,to,label?}]}] for any explanatory relationship: a taxonomy, mechanism, causal/control loop, process, trade-off, or argument map. When a review or artifact intent requires rows, columns, or direction, layout is mandatory and must encode that requirement; never leave required geometry only in discussion prose. Each diagram needs 3--10 short nodes and only relationships supported by its cited corpus. Add concept-illustration only when it is explicitly selected, the optional Nano Banana backend is enabled, and it provides orientation rather than evidence. Never select corpus bookkeeping, source inventories, DOI/venue listings, or a decorative chart.

The same JSON also supports a declarative figure-spec contract: timelines:[{id,title,caption,insight,placement:{section_id,discussion},source_ids:[three or more existing classified source ids]}] and table_specs:[{id,kind:<agent-chosen reader purpose>,comparative?:true|false,title,caption,insight,placement:{section_id,discussion},headers:[2--6 labels],rows:[{cells:[one per header],source_ids:[one or more existing classified source ids]}]}]. The agent chooses whether a timeline, table, diagram, verified numeric plot, imported empirical figure, or no artifact best serves the paper. Timelines derive dates and coordinates from verified metadata; table_specs derive the generated CSV, Markdown, longtable TeX, caption, label, and placement from this contract. Never supply raw TeX, plot code, arbitrary numbers, unsupported ratings, or unknown source ids. Every artifact you select needs an insight stating why a reader needs it; a legacy concept_map takes insight too, and a verified metadata plot takes its framing from metadata_plots:[{metric:publication_year|citation_depth|venue,insight,title?,caption?}]. An artifact with no insight fails the release gate rather than borrowing a generic one.
Place each artifact in the section whose argument it supports. Do not create an appendix-style generated-artifacts section.

Cite `[codebase:<id>]` or `[codebase:<id>:path#Lx-Ly]`; never claim execution results unless a verified empirical result artifact is supplied.

This is a repository-study paper. Write concept_map as a pinned-repository system architecture diagram: title/caption must say architecture or system architecture; nodes identify repository components/interfaces and edges identify data, control, or trust-boundary relationships. Ground labels in evidence/codebase-context.md, place it in the architecture section, and never depict inferred execution results. This architecture diagram is required for release.

Follow the injected project brief for audience, target length, and style. Do not cite a URL/file directly from the brief: recognized scholarly links enter through authoritative reference seeds and may be cited only after they appear in the section evidence packet; all other links/files remain contextual leads. Cite factual claims only with exact packet chunk ids.

Write complete reader-facing prose for this section, aiming for its outline.json target_words allocation. Do not emit a scaffold, source inventory, or a shorter placeholder merely because later revision exists.

Do not emit Markdown pipe tables, hand-numbered Table/Figure references, or prose pretending to be a diagram. The artifact builder owns captions, labels, table layout, and rendered figures; explain the comparison or relationship in prose and let the placed artifact carry the formal reference.

Use inline `$...$` or display `$$...$$` notation when it clarifies a sourced definition, objective, comparison, or analytical claim. Define every symbol in nearby prose and cite the supporting packet immediately before or after it. A literature-derived equation must be attributed; an author-created formalization must be labelled as a definition, model, or illustrative bound with its assumptions and must not be called a theorem, result, or empirical finding. Never add decorative equations or imply an experiment not supported by the evidence packet.
For research prose, cite only exact chunk ids from the injected evidence packet: [source:<source-id>:p<paragraph>]. A generic [source:<source-id>] marker is not enough for publication validation.
Do not cite a source merely because it appears in source_ids. If no packet chunk supports a factual claim, remove or qualify the claim.

Never use the word "packet" (or "evidence packet", "supplied packet") in manuscript prose. When evidence is absent, write "not reported by the cited source" or "outside this paper's scope," grounded in the claim's later_use/cross_task_transfer/meta_improvement status field — never a description of what the extraction pipeline happened to contain.

stages.title: Write research-paper abstract
instructions: Write paper/abstract.md as 150--250 words of reader-facing survey prose: the research problem, scope and selection basis, organizing contribution, main synthesis, and principal limitation or open question. Do not mention LongWrite, agents, prompts, or workflow mechanics. Do not use citations, source markers, headings other than an optional '# Abstract', or unsupported claims.

stages.title: Baseline simulated peer review
instructions: Treat every metadata-only or missing-evidence citation in reports/evidence-audit.md as a major review finding. Do not reward prose whose factual claims are not backed by exact evidence-packet chunk citations.

Review the rendered PDF hierarchy, placed figures, placed tables, captions, and in-text references. A file path or literal [source:...] marker printed in the manuscript is a blocking artifact defect, not a figure, table, or reader-facing citation.

Reward a well-designed explanatory diagram, source-grounded timeline, or qualitative comparison matrix when it makes the manuscript's argument more legible than prose. Review these for a clear analytical takeaway, source grounding, readable labels, and non-redundancy. For every equation, verify nearby symbol definitions and a literature citation or an explicit author-formalization label with stated assumptions; treat an unsupported theorem, conjecture, quantitative chart, or percentage as a major finding. Judge under-use as well as over-use: where a section argues a comparison across several sources in prose that a reader would follow far more easily as a table or diagram, say so and name the sections and the axis being compared. Do not ask for an artifact merely to raise a count, and never for one the cited evidence cannot support.
Treat a failing reviews/visual-qa.json as an independently verified major/critical artifact finding. Do not award a high review score while its page-specific legibility defects remain unresolved.

Use the injected project brief and outline.json as the length contract. Treat a manuscript materially below its total target or a section materially below its target_words as a release-blocking finding; name the sections and the evidence-grounded expansion needed, never recommend filler.

stages.title: Measure how far the persona reviews disagree
Resolve a material disagreement between persona reviews
instructions: reports/review-disagreement.json names the personas whose overall scores are furthest apart and by how much. reviews/scorecard.json carries every persona's per-dimension scores and summary.
Read the manuscript passages the disagreeing personas actually cite before deciding. An adjudication that restates the spread without examining the work is not a resolution.

Write ONLY reviews/adjudication/review_score.json as {version:1,by,at,status,resolved_score?,scorecard_digest,rationale}. Copy scorecard_digest verbatim from reports/review-disagreement.json: it binds your ruling to the exact scorecard you read, so a later review round cannot inherit it. `by` names you as the adjudicating role; `rationale` states which reading you found better supported and why, in the reviewers' own terms.

status is exactly one of resolved or unresolved. `resolved` REQUIRES resolved_score: the score on the reviewers' own 0-10 rubric that the dispute settles at, which becomes the recorded value for this metric. Do not restate the median — if the median was already right, say so and give it as the resolved_score.

resolved_score must lie between the lowest and highest persona overall in reports/review-disagreement.json. You are choosing between the readings on the table; a number outside them settles a different argument.

`unresolved` is a real answer and you may not name a score with it. Use it when the disagreement cannot be settled on the evidence available; the metric then stays unavailable and an operator is told you examined it and why it could not be closed.

You are resolving a disagreement about the manuscript, not changing the rubric and not lowering the target. Choosing a resolved_score outside the range the personas actually reported is not an adjudication of their dispute.

Diagnose an objective that repeated repair could not meet
instructions: Read repair/diagnosis-packet.json. It carries this objective's whole history: every strategy already attempted with its outcome, every value already measured, whether the target is reachable at all, and the packet the failed action received.
Write ONLY reviews/diagnosis.json as {version:1,objective,decision,detail,next_effect?,next_capability?,operator_question?}.

decision is exactly one of retry_with_different_effect (name next_effect), escalate_capability (name a registered next_capability), operator_required (state the operator_question), or target_infeasible.
Choose a strategy that has NOT already been attempted; the packet lists what has. Repeating one spends a round to relearn what the journal already records.

You may not lower or restate the target. An objective met by redefining it is not met. If the target cannot be reached with the evidence available, say target_infeasible and explain what would have to change.

instructions: Deterministically sample substantive cited claims from every section. Use stable sample ids like claim-001.

Write reviews/claim-judgments.jsonl with TWO independent JSONL judgments per sample_id, reviewer_id values reviewer_a and reviewer_b, and fields {sample_id,reviewer_id,source_id,chapter,claim,evidence_locators,prompt_hash,model,runtime,verdict,rationale,subject_key,polarity}. verdict must be entailed, partial, or unsupported.

subject_key is a short, normalized lowercase-hyphenated id naming the specific real-world mechanism or finding the claim is about (e.g. "stale-constraint-provenance-mechanism"), not the source or the chapter. Two claims about the same mechanism MUST share the same subject_key even when worded differently, so contradictions across sections can be detected automatically. polarity is affirms, denies, or qualifies: affirms asserts the mechanism holds, denies asserts the evidence cannot establish it or that it does not hold, qualifies neither affirms nor denies but narrows scope.
Judge the exact evidence packet/chunk locators, not source metadata. Any disagreement must be routed to human review or revision before release.

tool_catalog.title: Expand research evidence for an identified coverage gap
instructions: research/retrieval-brief.json lists the landmark targets the ledger still has no source for, with how many times each has been attempted. Search for those FIRST: a target listed there is one this paper has already decided it needs, and a round that returns other sources leaves the same coverage gap open.

tool_catalog.title: Re-derive the bibliography from the classified corpus
instructions: The bibliography and citation plan are DERIVED from sources/classified_sources.jsonl. An inconsistency between them and the corpus is repaired by re-deriving them, never by editing the derived file.

tool_catalog.title: Rebuild section citation allocations from the outline and corpus
instructions: Regenerate only sources/citation_plan.jsonl from the current real outline sections and classified corpus. Do not alter bibliography or source metadata.

tool_catalog.title: Re-derive source identity and metadata from the corpus the records name
instructions: Identity is re-derived from the corpus rather than edited in place: a record whose metadata disagrees with the source it names is corrected by reading the source again.

tool_catalog.title: Reopen the approved outline for a structural correction
instructions: This action is authorized only because the validated plan selected reopen_outline. Rewrite outline.md and outline.json to repair the named major/critical structural, scope, or taxonomy defect. Once chapters/*.md exist, section IDs are immutable manuscript identity keys: preserve the exact existing ID sequence and section count. You may change titles, ordering logic, and chapter purposes, but never rename, add, remove, or repurpose an ID; an ID change requires an explicit chapter-migration action, which this tool does not have.

Write feedback/outline-revision.md with the exact action-plan findings addressed, the structural change, and any remaining evidence limitation. Never select corpus bookkeeping, source inventories, DOI/venue listings, or a decorative chart.

The same JSON also supports a declarative figure-spec contract: timelines:[{id,title,caption,insight,placement:{section_id,discussion},source_ids:[three or more existing classified source ids]}] and table_specs:[{id,kind:<agent-chosen reader purpose>,comparative?:true|false,title,caption,insight,placement:{section_id,discussion},headers:[2--6 labels],rows:[{cells:[one per header],source_ids:[one or more existing classified source ids]}]}]. The agent chooses whether a timeline, table, diagram, verified numeric plot, imported empirical figure, or no artifact best serves the paper. Timelines derive dates and coordinates from verified metadata; table_specs derive the generated CSV, Markdown, longtable TeX, caption, label, and placement from this contract. Never supply raw TeX, plot code, arbitrary numbers, unsupported ratings, or unknown source ids. Every artifact you select needs an insight stating why a reader needs it; a legacy concept_map takes insight too, and a verified metadata plot takes its framing from metadata_plots:[{metric:publication_year|citation_depth|venue,insight,title?,caption?}]. An artifact with no insight fails the release gate rather than borrowing a generic one.
Place each artifact in the section whose argument it supports. Do not create an appendix-style generated-artifacts section.

Use reviews/action-plan.json, reviews/artifact-plan.json, and reviews/scorecard.json to repair only selected artifact findings. Preserve valid placements. Write a strict figures/placement-plan.json; do not edit manuscript prose, build outputs, or undeclared artifacts. Remove any artifact that is pipeline telemetry, a source inventory, or decorative rather than analytical. A validated metadata_plot is rendered from verified metadata only when it is essential to a stated reader-facing claim; do not invent plot values or use Nano Banana as evidence.

For new survey-native artifacts, use table_specs for source-bound comparison/taxonomy/evidence matrices and timelines for source-selected milestones. The builder validates all source IDs and derives timeline years; do not insert raw TeX, chart code, coordinates, or unsupported numerical results.

For every repaired diagram whose review specifies rows, columns, or direction, encode that requirement structurally as layout:{kind:'grid',columns:1|2|3} or layout:{kind:'flow',direction:'left_to_right'|'top_to_bottom'}. Do not leave required geometry only in placement.discussion. LongWrite deterministically renders grid layouts and validates the layout contract before rebuilding the PDF.

Configured repositories are pinned codebase evidence, not scholarly literature. Use evidence/codebase-analysis.json as the validated architecture dossier and inspect its exact file/line locators before making a repository claim. Cite `[codebase:<id>]` or `[codebase:<id>:path#Lx-Ly]`; never claim execution results unless a verified empirical result artifact is supplied.

Evaluate whether the manuscript's architecture, entrypoint, interface, data/control-flow, configuration, trust-boundary, and limitation claims agree with evidence/codebase-analysis.json and its exact locators. Treat missing or contradictory repository grounding as a measurable evidence/structure defect; do not award credit for merely mentioning the repository.
